name: Methylmalonic Acidemia Due to Methylmalonyl-CoA Epimerase Deficiency
aliases: Methylmalonic Aciduria due to Methylmalonyl-CoA Epimerase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Methylmalonic Acidemia

criteria.description: Elevated methylmalonic acid levels in plasma or urine
Reduced or absent methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase enzyme activity in fibroblasts or liver tissue
Identification of pathogenic variants in the MCEE gene
Presence of metabolic acidosis and neurological symptoms consistent with MMA

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated methylmalonic acid plus either confirmed enzyme deficiency or pathogenic MCEE gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe metabolic acidosis with elevated methylmalonic acid
searchTerms: severe acid buildup in blood with high methylmalonic acid
acidic blood and increased methylmalonic acid levels
delayed development with low muscle tone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent episodes of vomiting and lethargy during metabolic crises
searchTerms: frequent vomiting and tiredness during metabolic crisis
episodes of nausea and lethargy in metabolic decompensation
recurrent sickness with vomiting and low energy
low blood sugar during metabolic crisis

laboratory: Elevated methylmalonic acid in plasma and urine
Metabolic acidosis with increased anion gap
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia abnormalities
other: Reduced methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: Mutase deficiency involves MUT gene mutations
Elevated propionic acid rather than methylmalonic acid
Mutations in PCCA or PCCB genes
Different acylcarnitine profile with elevated C3

redFlags: Severe metabolic acidosis refractory to standard treatment
Rapid neurological deterioration during metabolic crises
Early onset of metabolic decompensation in neonates
references: Fenton WA, Gravel RA, Rosenblatt DS. Disorders of Propionate and Methylmalonate Metabolism. In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th edition. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
Orphanet: Methylmalonic acidemia due to methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase deficiency. ORPHA:308425.
Watkins D, Rosenblatt DS. Inherited disorders of vitamin B12 metabolism: a current perspective. Biochimie. 2011.
